# ProgressBar

Figma: [04j. ProgressBar](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-920) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-07-26

A linear horizontal bar that fills proportionally with a value (0–100%). Used for funding progress, completion indicators, file uploads, profile setup. 30 variants encode 3 sizes (sm/md/lg = 4/8/12px) × 5 tones (brand/success/warning/error/neutral) × 2 directions (LTR / RTL). The inner fill rectangle (named "fill") is resized by the designer or animated by code to represent the current value.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/progress-bar/reference.png`

### ProgressBar

Linear bar that fills to a known percentage, with an optional label row (Label, Value). The core use is deal funding progress such as 78% funded, plus profile completion and uploads.

Level: atom · Part of: CardDeal, File Item with Progress

Use when:
- Funded % on a CardDeal or deal page (Tone=brand)
- Profile or KYC completion percentage
- File upload progress, switching Tone to success or error by outcome
- Goal amount progress toward a target

Don't use when:
- Unknown duration: use ProgressBar_Indeterminate or a Spinner
- Discrete steps (3 of 5 documents): use ProgressSegment composition
- Named onboarding milestones with a reward: use MilestoneProgress
- Dated stages: use TimelineRow
- Loading a layout: use Skeleton primitives

Accessibility: role=progressbar with aria-valuenow; Value text uses Western digits (70%); fill grows from the right in RTL.

### MilestoneProgress

Rich milestone bar with four swappable milestone icons, gradient fill, knob and a reward end-cap, built for profile completion journeys (profile, KYC, preferences, email) that end in a reward.

Level: molecule

Use when:
- Home-screen profile completion hero card (Size=Large)
- Compact pinned reminder of the same journey (Size=Small)
- Reward moment after the last milestone (Value=fullGift, briefly fullParty)

Don't use when:
- Plain percentage such as funded %: use ProgressBar
- More than four steps: use a ProgressSegment composition
- Dated stages: use TimelineRow
- Goal savings progress: use GoalTracker

Accessibility: Announce milestone text ("Step 2 of 4, verify identity"); icons are decorative; respect reduced motion for fullParty.

### ProgressBar_Indeterminate

Indeterminate linear bar that sweeps continuously (Phase 0 to 3 loop) when an operation is running but progress cannot be measured.

Level: atom

Use when:
- Waiting on a bank or Nafath/Abshir verification response with no progress signal
- Top-of-screen activity bar while a list refreshes
- Background sync where a bar fits better than a spinner

Don't use when:
- Known percentage: use ProgressBar
- Short waits under 500ms or inside a button: use SpinnerRing or Button loading state
- Layout loading: use SkeletonLine and SkeletonBlock

Accessibility: role=progressbar without aria-valuenow plus a text status; stop animation under prefers-reduced-motion.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Size | `size` | variant | sm, md, lg | sm |
| Phase | `phase` | variant | 0, 1, 2, 3 | 0 |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

ProgressBar is the linear progress primitive. Use it whenever you need to show "x% complete" along a horizontal axis - funding progress, file uploads, profile setup, KYC progression, time-elapsed indicators. It is intentionally narrow: one shape (pill-ended rectangle), three sizes, five tones. For step-based progress (3 of 5 done) use ProgressSegment instead. For circular progress use RadialProgress.

### When to reach for ProgressBar

- A continuous percentage between 0 and 100 (deal funded 78%, profile complete 35%).
- A loading state with known duration (file upload 4 of 8 MB).
- A goal tracker where the goal is a single number (target 50,000 ﷼, current 12,500 ﷼).

### When NOT to use ProgressBar

- Step-based flows where steps are discrete and individually meaningful (3 of 5 KYC steps done) - use ProgressSegment.
- Compact circular progress indicators inside a card or widget - use RadialProgress.
- Multi-stage journeys with timing and metadata (deal payment timeline) - use Timeline.
- Indeterminate loading (waiting for an API response with no known duration) - use a Spinner pattern (not currently in Syntropy).

### Anatomy

A ProgressBar has two parts: the TRACK (the full-width pill shape representing 100%) and the FILL (the inner rectangle representing the current value). The fill is left-aligned by default and clips to the track. Both elements use Radius/Full so they read as pill ends.

| Track (background pill) - bg/{tone}-subtle | Fill (inner bar, named "fill") - bg/{tone} |
| --- | --- |

### Properties (added 2026-06-09)

The bar lives inside a vertical auto-layout container. Above the bar sits a labelRow with a Label text node (left) and a Value text node (right), justified space-between. Three instance properties expose this row to designers: Label (TEXT, default "Funded"), Value (TEXT, default "50%"), and showLabel (BOOLEAN, default false). When showLabel is false the labelRow collapses entirely and the bar renders at its original height - no visual change to existing instances placed before this update.

> **Tip:** Fill width is set manually. Select the inner "fill" rectangle on an instance and drag its right edge or set its width in the right panel. The Value text property is purely cosmetic - it does not drive the fill width. This is the industry-standard pattern (Carbon, MUI, Polaris all do the same) because Figma TEXT properties cannot drive rectangle dimensions without 100+ width-step variants per (Size × Tone) combination. Keeping fill manual lets one component cover every percentage from 0–100 without 165+ variants.

### Sizes

Three sizes scale the visual prominence. Use sm for compact indicators tucked into cards, md as the default for most cases, lg for hero progress bars that should grab attention.

sm (4px) - compact indicators in card footers, inline in KeyValue rows

md (8px) - default; most common (profile completion, file upload, funding %)

lg (12px) - hero progress in a celebration card or key dashboard widget

### Indeterminate state

When progress cannot be measured (an operation is happening but we cannot tell how far along it is), use the ProgressBar_Indeterminate set instead of the determinate ProgressBar. It is a separate component set located alongside this one on the 04j page. Three sizes (sm/md/lg, matching the determinate sibling) and four Phase variants per size. Each variant has a built-in Smart Animate reaction cycling Phase=0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 0 over 1.2 seconds. Drop an instance into a mockup at Phase=0 (the default) and press Play (▶) - the fill sweeps across the track continuously.

Animation keyframes (Size=md)

Phase 0 · t=0%

Phase 1 · t=25%

Phase 2 · t=50%

Phase 3 · t=75%

> **Tip:** When to use indeterminate vs determinate: use determinate (the main ProgressBar) whenever you can measure progress - file upload bytes received, form steps completed, etc. Use indeterminate only when the duration is genuinely unknown (a server query, an external API call where the backend gives no progress signal). For very short indeterminate operations under 500ms, prefer a Loader spinner (05f) instead - a sweeping progress bar that flashes for 200ms looks broken.

### Tones

Five tones convey semantic meaning. Pick the tone based on what the progress means, not what the data is.

Tone = brand

Default. Use for general progress: deal funding, profile completion, multi-step flows. The brand green signals "things are progressing as expected".

Tone = success

Use for achievement-flavored progress: goal trackers, milestones reached, "you saved X this month". Brighter than brand to convey accomplishment.

Tone = warning

Use for slow or at-risk progress: settlement past due, KYC documents missing, time running out. Amber says "needs attention".

Tone = error

Use for failed or critical states: upload failed, validation blocked, deadline missed. Reserve for true error - overusing makes the surface read as broken.

Tone = neutral

Use for non-status progress: pagination indicators, "5 of 12 items loaded", read-time bars. The black/gray says "this is a measurement, not a status".

### Direction (LTR / RTL)

ProgressBar is direction-aware. Direction (LTR / RTL) is a variant axis, so the set now holds 30 variants - Size × Tone × Direction. Use LTR for Latin screens and RTL for Arabic; the label row and the fill mirror automatically.

Direction = LTR - label left, value right, fill grows left → right

Direction = RTL - label right, value left, fill grows right → left

- RTL mirrors the label row: label sits on the RIGHT, value on the LEFT (the LTR order is reversed).
- The fill anchors to the right edge and grows right → left, so progress reads from the RTL start.
- Label, Value and the showLabel boolean behave identically in both directions - only layout flips.
- Pick Direction per screen locale; don’t rotate or manually flip an LTR instance.
- Tone and Size are independent of Direction - every Size × Tone pairing exists in both LTR and RTL.

> **Tip:** Pair Direction=RTL with an Arabic Label. Value numerals stay Western (e.g. 70%) per the DS number convention - only the layout mirrors, not the digits.

### In context - common patterns

Three canonical ProgressBar patterns from Safqah surfaces.

### Pattern 1: Deal funding progress

A deal card shows funding progress as a horizontal bar above the call-to-action. The bar uses brand tone (because funding-in-progress is the default semantic, not "success"). The numeric label sits above the bar.

Riyadh Commercial Complex - Sukuk SAF-2025-Q3-014

| 3,920,000 ﷼ of 5,000,000 ﷼ | 78% |
| --- | --- |

### Pattern 2: Profile completion (inline in card)

A compact "complete your profile" reminder card uses the sm size to stay unobtrusive. Sits in a sidebar or under the main hero. Switches to success tone at 100%.

Complete your profile - 65%

Add your CMA license to unlock premium deals

### Pattern 3: File upload (tone changes by state)

Document upload progress changes tone by state: brand while uploading, success when complete, error if upload failed. The state mapping IS the design.

salary_cert.pdf - uploading (54%)

bank_statement.pdf - upload complete

id_scan.jpg - upload failed (retry)

### Code examples - Flutter

Reference implementation. Production code lives in lib/design_system/progress_bar/.

### Basic usage

```dart
// Default 50% progress
const SyntropyProgressBar(
  value: 0.5,
  size: ProgressBarSize.md,
  tone: ProgressBarTone.brand,
)

// Funding indicator on a deal card
SyntropyProgressBar(
  value: deal.fundedAmount / deal.targetAmount,
  size: ProgressBarSize.md,
  tone: deal.isFullyFunded ? ProgressBarTone.success : ProgressBarTone.brand,
)

// File upload with tone changing by state
SyntropyProgressBar(
  value: upload.bytesUploaded / upload.totalBytes,
  size: ProgressBarSize.sm,
  tone: switch (upload.state) {
    UploadState.uploading => ProgressBarTone.brand,
    UploadState.complete => ProgressBarTone.success,
    UploadState.failed => ProgressBarTone.error,
  },
)
```

### Implementation

```dart
class SyntropyProgressBar extends StatelessWidget {
  final double value;        // 0.0 to 1.0
  final ProgressBarSize size;
  final ProgressBarTone tone;

  const SyntropyProgressBar({
    super.key,
    required this.value,
    this.size = ProgressBarSize.md,
    this.tone = ProgressBarTone.brand,
  }) : assert(value >= 0.0 && value <= 1.0);

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final theme = SyntropyTheme.of(context);
    final height = switch (size) {
      ProgressBarSize.sm => 4.0,
      ProgressBarSize.md => 8.0,
      ProgressBarSize.lg => 12.0,
    };
    
    final fillColor = switch (tone) {
      ProgressBarTone.brand => theme.bg.brand.primary,
      ProgressBarTone.success => theme.bg.success,
      ProgressBarTone.warning => theme.bg.warning,
      ProgressBarTone.error => theme.bg.error,
      ProgressBarTone.neutral => theme.bg.inverse,
    };
    
    final trackColor = switch (tone) {
      ProgressBarTone.brand => theme.bg.brand.primarySubtle,
      ProgressBarTone.success => theme.bg.successSubtle,
      ProgressBarTone.warning => theme.bg.warningSubtle,
      ProgressBarTone.error => theme.bg.errorSubtle,
      ProgressBarTone.neutral => theme.bg.base,
    };

    return Semantics(
      label: 'Progress',
      value: '${(value * 100).round()}%',
      child: ClipRRect(
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(height / 2),
        child: Container(
          height: height,
          color: trackColor,
          child: Align(
            alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
            child: FractionallySizedBox(
              widthFactor: value,
              child: Container(color: fillColor),
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Migration from Global_Design_System

The legacy Safqah library (Global_Design_System) contained 9 progress-bar components with inconsistent naming and overlapping responsibilities. Syntropy v2.0 consolidates them into three clear components: ProgressBar (linear), ProgressSegment (segmented), and RadialProgress (circular).

### Legacy → Syntropy v2.0 mapping

Legacy: progress bar / Progress bar (duplicate, case-only difference)

→  ProgressBar (Size=md, Tone=brand)

Use the new variant axes for size and tone instead of two near-identical components.

Legacy: OutProgressBar

→  ProgressBar (Size=md, Tone=success or neutral)

Maps to a completed/outgoing-state progress. Use tone to convey "done".

Legacy: Goal progress bar

→  NOT a ProgressBar - it is a caption text row. Use a Text element with a separate ProgressBar above it.

The legacy component is misnamed. The actual goal bar visual was rendered ad-hoc per screen.

Legacy: Raidal_progressBar / Raidal_progressBar-s (note: "Raidal" was a typo)

→  RadialProgress (Size=md or lg, choose Tone)

Typo corrected. -s suffix collapses into the Size axis.

Legacy: R-progressBar / R-progressBar-s

→  RadialProgress (Size=md or lg)

These were duplicate radials with shorter naming prefix. All consolidated to RadialProgress.

Legacy: Documents-progress-bar

→  Progress (composition of ProgressSegment instances)

Document upload stepped indicator now uses the explicit segment composition pattern.

Legacy: Complete profile progress (5 + 6-variant component sets in Onboarding Draft page)

→  Composition of RadialProgress + Card + KeyValue rows + Button. NOT a single component.

The legacy component conflated radial + checklist + CTA into one unwieldy variant set. Compose these atoms instead.

Legacy: Years goal progress (886:13214)

→  Stack of multiple ProgressBar instances in a vertical layout, each representing one year.

The legacy version embedded layout and content directly. The new pattern composes per-row ProgressBars.

> **Info:** The legacy components are not removed from the Global_Design_System library - they continue to work in old designs. New designs should use Syntropy v2.0 ProgressBar, ProgressSegment, or RadialProgress. When refactoring an old screen, replace each legacy instance one-at-a-time with the appropriate new component.

### Notes from the maintainer

Design decisions and constraints for the next maintainer.

> **Info:** The inner fill rectangle is named "fill" (lowercase) and lives directly inside the component. Production code can target it by name when animating progress. Figma instances will preserve this name in nested overrides.

> **Info:** Brand tone uses bg/brand/primary, NOT bg/progress. The bg/progress token in the Syntropy DS resolves to a secondary PURPLE color (intended for an alternate progress context), which would be wrong for a brand-default progress bar. The brand tone correctly uses the main green primary.

> **Info:** Progress value is NOT a variant axis. Designers resize the inner fill rectangle to whatever width represents their value (50% = TRACK_WIDTH/2). Encoding 0/25/50/75/100 as variants would have created 5x the component count for marginal benefit. Production code drives fill width via percentage; designers handle it with manual resize.

> **Info:** No indeterminate/striped variant. Safqah backends always know the progress value, so we never need an animated indeterminate loading bar. If a future use case appears (waiting for a long API call with no progress signal), add a separate Spinner pattern - do not add a striped variant here.

> **Info:** The neutral tone uses bg/inverse (dark) for the fill, NOT a gray. This is intentional - neutral progress bars (e.g. read-time indicator) should still feel intentional. A gray fill on a gray track is too subtle to register.

> **Warning:** For RTL contexts, the fill should grow from the RIGHT edge instead of the LEFT. The current ProgressBar component does not encode this - designers must mirror the fill rectangle manually OR Production Flutter code uses Directionality to flip the alignment.

### Overview

MilestoneProgress is a richer progress bar than the standard ProgressBar. Use it when progress has named milestones, when the journey itself is the story, and when the user benefits from seeing what they have unlocked and what is coming next. The canonical use case is the Safqah profile completion / onboarding bar - 4 milestones (profile → KYC → preferences → email confirmed) culminating in a reward.

### When to reach for MilestoneProgress

- Multi-step onboarding flows with named milestones (4 specific stages, each with its own icon).
- Profile/account completion where each milestone unlocks something (verification → premium deals → notifications).
- Reward-based progressions where reaching 100% means earning something (cashback, badge, tier upgrade).
- Anywhere the user benefits from celebration at completion - the fullGift and fullParty states make the moment.

### When NOT to use MilestoneProgress

- Simple percentage progress (78% funded) - use ProgressBar.
- More than 4 distinct milestones - the icons row gets cramped. Use Progress (segmented) for 5-10 step counts.
- Sequential timelines with dates and amounts - use Timeline.
- Compact widgets where the full milestone bar would dominate - use RadialProgress for compact progress, or Small size if the milestones fit.

### Sample at-a-glance

Value = 25

Value = 50

Value = 75

Value = fullGift

Value = fullParty

### Anatomy

MilestoneProgress (Large) is composed of six layered elements, in this stacking order from bottom to top: track → fill → step dots → knob → end-cap → milestone icons. Each plays a specific role in communicating progress.

### Element breakdown

- Milestone icons (top row): 4 icons representing each major step. Active milestones (reached) display at full opacity; upcoming milestones are at 35% opacity. INSTANCE_SWAP - designers swap each icon per use case.
- Track: the full-width pill-shaped background (bg/brand/primary-subtle). Always 43px tall on Large, 8px on Small.
- Fill: the gradient pill that grows as progress increases. Gradient from bg/brand/primary (lighter top) to bg/brand/darkest (darker bottom-right) for a tactile feel.
- Step dots: 4 small dots on the empty portion marking upcoming milestones. 35% opacity. Hidden for completed segments (the fill covers them).
- Knob: a 13px circular indicator at the leading edge of the fill, with a subtle drop shadow. Shows "you are here". Hidden at 100%/fullGift/fullParty (no more progress to indicate).
- End-cap: a 43px circle on the trailing edge of the bar, holding a reward icon. Star preview (40% opacity) when in-progress, bag-dollar at 100%, bag-dollar at fullGift, star at fullParty.

### Value states

Seven discrete Values cover the progress lifecycle and reward states. Each represents a specific moment in the user journey.

Value = 0

Empty start. No milestones reached. All icons at low opacity, no fill, knob absent, end-cap shows a faint star (a preview of the reward).

Value = 25

First milestone reached. Icon 1 at full opacity, fill spans roughly 25%, knob at the leading edge, step dots show 3 upcoming milestones.

Value = 50

Halfway. Icons 1-2 active, fill spans 50%, knob at the leading edge.

Value = 75

Three of four milestones reached. Icons 1-3 active, fill spans 75%, knob at the leading edge.

Value = 100

All milestones complete. All 4 icons at full opacity, fill spans the full track, knob hidden (no more progress), end-cap shows a bag-dollar icon (reward incoming).

Value = fullGift

Reward unlocked. Identical to 100 but the bag-dollar icon is at full prominence - signals "your reward is here". Use immediately after the user finishes the last milestone.

Value = fullParty

Celebration moment. End-cap shows a star - pure visual celebration. Use briefly during a reward animation/transition, then transition back to a calmer state.

### Sizes

Two sizes serve different contexts. Use Large when the milestone story IS the screen (onboarding hero card); use Small when progress sits secondary to other content (footer, sidebar, inline reminder).

Small - 24px tall, 4-segment graduated bar

No icons or end-cap. Each completed segment is solid brand green; upcoming segments are at low opacity. Use when the milestone bar is secondary content - inline in a card footer, a sidebar reminder, a header progress indicator.

Large - 71px tall, full milestone bar

Includes the 4 milestone icons, gradient fill, knob, step dots, and end-cap reward circle. Use when the progress journey IS the focus of the screen - onboarding cards, profile completion heroes, account-setup CTAs.

### In context - common patterns

Three real Safqah patterns.

### Pattern 1: Profile completion hero (Large)

A dedicated card on the home screen invites the user to complete their profile. The Large MilestoneProgress is the focal element. The user clicks through onboarding milestones; each completion advances the Value, knob position, and unlocks the next icon. At completion the end-cap reveals the reward.

Complete your profile to unlock all features

Step 2 of 4 - Verify your identity

### Pattern 2: Compact reminder banner (Small)

After the user dismisses the hero card or scrolls past it, the Small variant lives in a compact banner pinned to the top of the home screen. Same milestones, less screen real estate.

Profile 50%

### Pattern 3: Arabic profile completion (RTL)

Saudi-market Arabic-first profile completion. RTL variant mirrors the bar - first milestone on the right, end-cap on the left, fill grows leftward. Reading flows naturally for Arabic users.

تقدمك في إتمام بياناتك

### Basic usage

```dart
// Large milestone bar at step 2 of 4 (LTR, English)
const SyntropyMilestoneProgress(
  size: MilestoneProgressSize.large,
  value: MilestoneProgressValue.v25,
  direction: TextDirection.ltr,
  icons: [
    Icon(SyntropyIcons.userSingle),
    Icon(SyntropyIcons.chartArea),
    Icon(SyntropyIcons.userCircle),
    Icon(SyntropyIcons.mailSolo),
  ],
)

// Celebration moment at completion
const SyntropyMilestoneProgress(
  size: MilestoneProgressSize.large,
  value: MilestoneProgressValue.fullParty,
  direction: TextDirection.ltr,
)

// Arabic RTL profile bar
const SyntropyMilestoneProgress(
  size: MilestoneProgressSize.large,
  value: MilestoneProgressValue.v75,
  direction: TextDirection.rtl,
  icons: [ /* same 4 icons; layout mirrors */ ],
)

// Small compact variant for sidebar/banner
const SyntropyMilestoneProgress(
  size: MilestoneProgressSize.small,
  value: MilestoneProgressValue.v50,
)
```

### Stateful animation

```dart
class ProfileCompletionBar extends StatefulWidget {
  final int currentMilestone; // 0-4
  final bool celebrating;
  
  const ProfileCompletionBar({
    super.key,
    required this.currentMilestone,
    this.celebrating = false,
  });

  @override
  State<ProfileCompletionBar> createState() => _ProfileCompletionBarState();
}

class _ProfileCompletionBarState extends State<ProfileCompletionBar>
    with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late AnimationController _controller;
  
  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    _controller = AnimationController(
      duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 600),
      vsync: this,
    );
    _controller.forward();
  }

  MilestoneProgressValue _resolveValue() {
    if (widget.celebrating) return MilestoneProgressValue.fullParty;
    return switch (widget.currentMilestone) {
      0 => MilestoneProgressValue.v0,
      1 => MilestoneProgressValue.v25,
      2 => MilestoneProgressValue.v50,
      3 => MilestoneProgressValue.v75,
      4 => MilestoneProgressValue.v100,
      _ => MilestoneProgressValue.v0,
    };
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return AnimatedBuilder(
      animation: _controller,
      builder: (context, child) => SyntropyMilestoneProgress(
        size: MilestoneProgressSize.large,
        value: _resolveValue(),
        icons: const [
          Icon(SyntropyIcons.userSingle),
          Icon(SyntropyIcons.chartArea),
          Icon(SyntropyIcons.userCircle),
          Icon(SyntropyIcons.mailSolo),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Migration from Product_Design / Global_Design_System

The legacy "Full-progress" component in the Product_Design file is the direct ancestor of this MilestoneProgress. It encoded the same idea - a milestone bar with icons, knob, and end-cap reward - but lived as a one-off rather than a proper design system component. MilestoneProgress brings it into Syntropy v2.0 with full variant axes, INSTANCE_SWAP icon props, and RTL support.

### Legacy → Syntropy v2.0 mapping

Legacy: Full-progress · Size=Small, Value=25 (in Product_Design file 0EsfJp3Tzwn4DgfoI7Z64l)

→  MilestoneProgress · Size=Small, Value=25, Direction=LTR

Identical 4-segment graduated bar.

Legacy: Full-progress · Size=Large, Value=25/50/75/100

→  MilestoneProgress · Size=Large, Value=25/50/75/100, Direction=LTR

All 4 progress states map directly. Knob position, fill width, step dots match.

Legacy: Full-progress · Value=full

→  MilestoneProgress · Value=fullGift

Renamed for clarity. "full" was ambiguous (full filled? full unlock?); "fullGift" makes the reward state explicit.

Legacy: Full-progress · Value=fullParty

→  MilestoneProgress · Value=fullParty

Same name. The celebration star moment.

Legacy: Hardcoded icons (user/chart/userCircle/mail) in legacy

→  INSTANCE_SWAP icon1/icon2/icon3/icon4 properties

Designers can now swap any of the 4 milestone icons per instance. Defaults are the same icons as legacy.

Legacy: No RTL variant in legacy

→  Direction=LTR | RTL

Adds full RTL support - bar mirrors, icons reverse order, fill grows from right edge.

Legacy: Hardcoded brand colors in legacy

→  All colors bound to Syntropy semantic tokens (bg/brand/primary, bg/brand/darkest, bg/brand/primary-subtle)

Dark mode and theme switching come for free once those modes are enabled on the collection.

> **Info:** The legacy Full-progress component remains in the Product_Design file for backwards compatibility. New designs should use Syntropy v2.0 MilestoneProgress. When refactoring an existing screen, replace each Full-progress instance one-at-a-time with the appropriate Syntropy variant.

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** The knob disappears at Value=100/fullGift/fullParty because there is no more progress to indicate. If a future design wants a persistent "you finished here" knob at completion, that is a new variant axis (HasKnob) - do not just always show it.

> **Info:** fullGift and fullParty are intentionally separate values, not a single "complete" state. They represent two distinct moments in the post-completion experience: fullGift = "your reward is here" (steady state), fullParty = "celebrating right now" (transient). Apps should typically use fullParty briefly (e.g. 2-3 seconds during a reward animation) then settle to fullGift.

> **Tip:** The 4 milestone icons are INSTANCE_SWAP properties (icon1/icon2/icon3/icon4). Defaults are user-single, chart-area, user-circle, mail-solo - the most common Safqah onboarding flow. For different flows (e.g. investment, KYC) designers swap each icon per instance.

> **Info:** In RTL mode, the icon ORDER reverses visually (icon4 on the far left becomes the visual first milestone). The component handles this automatically by mirroring positions. Designers do not need to manually reorder.

> **Warning:** The Small variant has NO icons, knob, or end-cap. It is a pure segmented bar. If you need icons or a reward indicator at small size, use the Large size in a smaller container - do not add complexity to Small.

> **Warning:** The fill gradient is hard-coded RGB (not bound to Syntropy variables). This is a known limitation - Figma's GRADIENT_LINEAR paint type does not support variable bindings on gradient stops at the time of build. When variable-bound gradients become possible, this should be the first component upgraded.

> **Info:** Step dots on the empty portion of the bar are at 35% opacity. They are intentionally subtle - the icons row above carries the primary "what is the next milestone" signal. The dots are a redundant visual cue, not the main affordance.
